title: Deep learning domain adaptation to understand physico-chemical processes from fluorescence spectroscopy small datasets and application to the oxidation of olive oil.
summary: Domain-adapted deep learning extracts oxidation-related information from fluorescence spectra of olive oil, linking spectroscopy to a specific food-chemistry process. The reviewed source supports this bounded result; external generalization, causal effects, and sustained operational impact remain unestablished where the source reports retrospective or internal evaluation.
ai_technology: Small experimental set of oils and oxidation stages; prediction error and comparison against measured chemical indicators are reported.
organization: Research and Development, TOELT LLC, 8600, Dübendorf, Switzerland

evidence.tested: Domain-adapted deep learning extracts oxidation-related information from fluorescence spectra of olive oil, linking spectroscopy to a specific food-chemistry process.
evidence.unknown: Authors identify a small-data limitation and an outlier oil; this supports a laboratory process result, not broad food-quality deployment.
evidence.ai_role: Small experimental set of oils and oxidation stages; prediction error and comparison against measured chemical indicators are reported.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
